name: Spicy Chicken Stew (Saiha)
ingredients: 500g chicken (bone-in, preferably thigh and drumsticks, cut into chunks)
1 cup fermented bamboo shoots (tung-ngam), drained and rinsed
8-10 green bird's eye chilies (slit lengthwise, adjust for heat)
1/2 cup fresh coriander leaves (chopped, for garnish)
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat until smoking. Add the chicken pieces and sear until golden brown on all sides (about 5 minutes). Remove and set aside.
2. In the same oil, add chopped onions and sauté until translucent (3-4 minutes). Add minced garlic and grated ginger, stirring for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add slit green chilies and fermented bamboo shoots. Sauté for 2 minutes to lightly caramelize the bamboo.
4. Return the chicken to the pot. Add turmeric powder and salt, and stir well to coat. Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes until they soften.
5. Pour in enough water to barely cover the chicken (about 2 cups). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until chicken is tender and flavors meld.
6. Uncover, increase heat to medium, and cook for 5-7 minutes to reduce the gravy slightly, stirring occasionally. Adjust salt and chili intensity.
7. Remove from heat, garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves, and serve steaming hot with steamed rice or traditional bamboo-steamed bread (chhangban).
description: A fiery, smoky symphony of bamboo and bird's eye chili that warms the soul like a Mizo hearth.
